correctness.rationale: The claim is finite and exhaustively checked. Two independently defined compatibility tests agree on every one of the 496 unordered pairs of length-five binary words. Exhaustive tests of every six-subset and every seven-subset prove that the maximum is six and that exactly six labeled maxima exist. An independent maximal-clique search returns the same six maxima. Perfectness, VT syndromes, shadow profiles, and natural-symmetry orbits are recomputed directly from those six codes.

value.rationale: Length five is the first block length at which the classical \(VT_0(n)\) family is nonlinear, while the optimum is already nontrivial. A complete equality classification at this threshold distinguishes canonical perfect VT optima from four equally large nonperfect codes, showing that maximum cardinality and perfect deletion coverage already diverge structurally at this smallest nonlinear VT length. The exact orbit and shadow-profile data are natural finite invariants useful for testing structural conjectures and exact algorithms on deletion codes.
